findings: Emscripten >= 3.1.27 default stack is 64 KB; swarm.c FlowUpdate puts 128 KB of queue arrays on the stack at 128x128 (must move to static in R1).
Lighting_Update walks every tile every frame: 19 us at 45x45, 217 us at 128x128 on the sandbox; a 37x37 window is about 9 us at any size (window it in R1).

The pocket pass (CarveToReachable) is an O(n^2) Dijkstra per carve: fine at 45x45, will not scale to 128x128; a heap or bucket queue is an R1 item (keep ties by lowest index if exact equality matters, it does not for statistics).
mid-math Pcg32::range_u32 uses a 64-bit threshold (2^64 mod n) instead of 2^32 mod n; harmless statistically, breaks bit-exact parity with exact Lemire.
mid-math Pcg32 streams of one seed share their first output with seq 1 and 2 (20,000 of 20,000); FgStream derives state and increment separately to avoid it. Docs say 'completely independent'.

Bit rows win clearly on spans (1.7-2.7x), bands (2.4-5.9x) and 3x3 pattern fits (2.1-5.7x); flood fill by bit wavefront only wins at 128 or with hardware popcount; a wide 4-lane hash is 1.4-2.7x but saves microseconds (docs/design/09 section 5).
Diagonal probe rays pass exactly through tile corners; the integer walk breaks the tie z first at all four diagonals (the old float code differed at 225 degrees).
